title: Continuous-depth Deep Gaussian Processes
claim: Plain deep stacks degrade sharply with depth and residual links only delay this, while continuous-depth variants stay robust and beat the baseline.
layout: 3x3 grid of line plots, metrics across columns, sweep variable down rows
description: A 3x3 grid of line plots with shaded one-standard-deviation bands. Columns are the metrics RMSE, NLL and MAE. The top row plots error against depth L for standard DGP (blue circles) and residual DGP (green triangles). DGP jumps sharply at L=3 and then stays flat, and its NLL rises further at L=10. Residual DGP stays low until L=5 and then degrades with wide uncertainty bands. The middle row sweeps J at T=1 for CDGP (purple) and FlowDGP (teal squares), with a dashed green line for the two-layer residual DGP reference. FlowDGP dips well below the reference at J=2-3 and then rises, while CDGP stays nearly flat and slightly below the reference. The bottom row sweeps T at J=3, and FlowDGP again rises with T. A shared legend sits at the bottom. The eye goes first to the sharp DGP jump in the top row.
caption: Toy regression results. Top: test root mean squared error (RMSE), negative log-likelihood (NLL), and mean absolute error (MAE) versus depth $L$ for standard DGP and residual DGP. Middle: CDGP and FlowDGP versus $J$ at fixed $T=1$, with the dashed line showing the two-layer residual DGP reference. Bottom: CDGP and FlowDGP versus $T$ at fixed $J=3$. Shaded regions denote one standard deviation across random seeds.
abstract: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) are appealing Bayesian regression models, but their standard discrete-depth parameterization often becomes harder to optimize as depth grows. We argue that depth is better treated as a latent continuous evolution than as a long discrete stack. We therefore propose a continuous-depth formulation in which the latent representation follows a stochastic differential equation with a depth-indexed drift family equipped with a GP-based prior. This reframes the core design choice as the prior placed on that family, rather than adopting a purely neural continuous-depth parameterization as in neural ODE or neural SDE models. We study two instantiations of this idea: CDGP, a direct GP prior over the state--depth drift, and FlowDGP, a flow-evolved prior that captures richer depth dependence at lower training cost. To motivate the redesign, we analyze how the single-sample DGP objective can become increasingly sensitive under repeated layer composition, while residual DGP is a useful first repair that still remains a finite discrete construction. We also give pathwise sensitivity analysis for the continuous-depth formulation. Experiments on synthetic, benchmark, and large-scale regression tasks show that residual DGP improves over plain DGP, while CDGP and FlowDGP provide a stronger overall story across the regimes we study.
